card.name: Start of Hal- drug names
card.fires_on: The piece 'Hal' (or 'hal') that begins a word, mostly the start of halogenated, halothane, haloperidol, halobetasol or halofantrine. It also fires on 'hal' in 'halve' before a dose of digoxin.

modes.label: Halogen and Halo- drug names
modes.description: 'Hal' opens a drug or drug-class name such as halogenated anesthetics, halothane, haloperidol, halobetasol or halofantrine, often right after a section number or heading.

modes.label: Halve a dose
modes.description: 'hal' starts the verb halve, in advice to cut the digoxin dose.
modes.example: Consider discontinuing digoxin. If digoxin treatment is continued,<< hal>>ve the dose of digoxin,

card.writes: Little clear output effect; it promotes a few odd pieces of words such as 'ophile' and 'bling', which fit word-internal continuations.
card.plain: It fires on the opening letters 'Hal' of drug names like halothane and haloperidol, and of the word halve.
